subproblem.title: Tilt-excess bound for the gradient term G(t) (step 7(b))
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N, W an n-varifold on U, P ∈ G(N,n) and y ∈ ℝ^N. Let ε ≥ 0, M ≥ 0, A > 0 and t > 0. Let h : ℝ^N → ℝ be any function, and φ : ℝ → [0,1] with φ(s) = 0 for every s ≥ A². Write t_P(S) for the operator norm of p_S − p_P, i.e. ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap(projectionLinearMap S − projectionLinearMap P)‖, and Dh := fderiv ℝ h. Assume (2'): ∫⁻_{B_{tA}(y)×G(N,n)} ofReal(t_P(S)) dW(z,S) ≤ ofReal(ε(tA)^n) in [0,∞] (an extended-real Lebesgue integral), where B_{tA}(y) = closedBall y (tA). Assume (grad): |Dh(z)[p_S(z − y)]| ≤ M·t_P(S)·|z − y| for all z ∈ ℝ^N and S ∈ G(N,n). Then |G(t)| ≤ M·A^{n+1}·ε·t^{n+1}, where G(t) := ∫ φ(|z − y|²/t²)·Dh(z)[p_S(z − y)] dW(z,S) is a Bochner integral.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (W : Varifold N n U) (P : Grassmannian N n) (y : Euclidean N) (ε M A t : ℝ) (h : Euclidean N → ℝ) (φ : ℝ → ℝ), 0 ≤ ε → 0 ≤ M → 0 < A → 0 < t → (∫⁻ z in closedBall y (t * A) ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), ENNReal.ofReal ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap z.2 - Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap P)‖ ∂W.measure) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (ε * (t * A) ^ n) → (∀ (z : Euclidean N) (S : Grassmannian N n), |fderiv ℝ h z (Grassmannian.project S (z - y))| ≤ M * ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap S - Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap P)‖ * ‖z - y‖) → (∀ s, 0 ≤ φ s ∧ φ s ≤ 1) → (∀ s, A ^ 2 ≤ s → φ s = 0) → |∫ p, φ (‖p.1 - y‖ ^ 2 / t ^ 2) * fderiv ℝ h p.1 (Grassmannian.project p.2 (p.1 - y)) ∂W.measure| ≤ M * A ^ (n + 1) * ε * t ^ (n + 1)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7(b) of the parent proof: the estimate of the gradient term by hypothesis (2r) at radius r = tA, stated for one radius.
Notation. w := z − y. t_P(S) := ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap(projectionLinearMap S − projectionLinearMap P)‖ ≥ 0. g(z,S) := φ(‖w‖²/t²)·Dh(z)[p_S w], so G(t) = ∫ g dW. K := B_{tA}(y) × G(N,n) = closedBall y (tA) ×ˢ univ, a measurable set. Note tA > 0.

1. Pointwise bound.
 - Let (z,S) ∈ K, i.e. ‖w‖ ≤ tA. Since 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, |φ(‖w‖²/t²)| ≤ 1. By (grad), |g(z,S)| ≤ 1·M·t_P(S)·‖w‖ ≤ M·(tA)·t_P(S), using M ≥ 0 and t_P(S) ≥ 0.
 - Let (z,S) ∉ K, i.e. ‖w‖ > tA > 0. Then ‖w‖² > (tA)², so ‖w‖²/t² > A², hence φ(‖w‖²/t²) = 0 and g(z,S) = 0.
 So for all (z,S), in [0,∞]: ofReal|g(z,S)| ≤ 1_K(z,S)·ofReal(M·tA)·ofReal(t_P(S)). Here ofReal(xy) = ofReal(x)·ofReal(y) is used with x = M·tA ≥ 0.

2. Lebesgue integral bound. The lower Lebesgue integral is monotone for arbitrary functions (lintegral_mono). K is measurable, so the indicator can be turned into a set integral (lintegral_indicator). The finite constant ofReal(M·tA) can be pulled out (lintegral_const_mul'). Hence
  ∫⁻ ofReal|g| dW ≤ ∫⁻ 1_K·ofReal(M·tA)·ofReal(t_P(S)) dW(z,S)
           = ofReal(M·tA)·∫⁻_K ofReal(t_P(S)) dW(z,S)
           ≤ ofReal(M·tA)·ofReal(ε(tA)^n) = ofReal(M·tA·ε(tA)^n).
 The last inequality is hypothesis (2'); the last equality uses M·tA ≥ 0.

3. Bochner integral. For every function g, ‖∫ g dW‖ ≤ (∫⁻ ofReal‖g‖ dW).toReal (norm_integral_le_lintegral_norm). This needs no integrability: a non-integrable g has Bochner integral 0. toReal is monotone on finite values (ENNReal.toReal_mono), and M·tA·ε(tA)^n ≥ 0 because ε ≥ 0 and M ≥ 0. So
  |G(t)| = |∫ g dW| ≤ (ofReal(M·tA·ε(tA)^n)).toReal = M·tA·ε·(tA)^n = M·A^{n+1}·ε·t^{n+1}. ∎
proof_key_steps: on B_{tA}(y) × G, |g| ≤ M·tA·t_P(S) by (grad) and |φ| ≤ 1; off it, φ = 0, so g = 0
∫⁻ ofReal|g| dW ≤ ofReal(M tA)·∫⁻_{B_{tA}(y)×G} t_P dW ≤ ofReal(M·tA·ε(tA)^n), by (2')
|∫ g dW| ≤ (∫⁻ ofReal|g| dW).toReal ≤ M·tA·ε(tA)^n = M·A^{n+1}·ε·t^{n+1}

audit.reason: The prose and type match, including arbitrary h and the explicitly explained totalized Bochner integral. The support estimate gives pointwise domination by M(tA)t_P. The pinned lintegral lemmas need no additional measurability, and the unconditional Bochner norm bound covers non-integrable functions. The finite ENNReal upper bound justifies toReal monotonicity, and the final algebra yields exactly M A^(n+1) ε t^(n+1). No circular reliance or missing proof step remains.
